text:
maya: Quick design thread — proposing an ‘anchor swap’ strategy for the left sidebar groups + breadcrumbs. Goal: let deep links target subpanels without expanding the whole tree on load. Thoughts?
kevin: curious — can you sketch the URL contract? e.g. will we use hash anchors or pathname segments?
maya: thinking `/console/models/12345?panel=metrics#deploy` for deep link -> opens Models > Model 12345, shows metrics panel, then scrolls to deploy anchor. Keep path stable so breadcrumbs reflect hierarchy.
devon: small accessibility concern: if we auto-scroll to an anchor we need to move keyboard focus to the heading (aria-describedby or tabindex) or NVDA users will lose context.
anna: agree w/ devon. Also need to ensure screen readers announce that a panel was opened. Suggest `role="region" aria-labelledby="panel-title"` + focus management when panel becomes visible.
sam: routing nit: mixing query param + hash is okay but can get weird with history/back behaviour. If user clicks back we should `history.replaceState` when toggling panel to avoid polluting backstack.
kevin: example: ```js
// open panel without creating history entry
const url = new URL(window.location);
url.searchParams.set('panel','metrics');
window.history.replaceState({}, '', url);
```
maya: nice. UX question: collapsed groups — do we auto-expand the leftnav group when deep link hits a child? Or do we show a small highlight and a toast with a jump link?
devon: auto-expand is more discoverable; but we must persist expansion only for the session, not write to a canonical URL that other devices will misinterpret.
anna: for keyboard users, expanding should also ensure the focused item is in DOM order before focusing. Avoid focus trap in closed groups.
sam: breadcrumbs: currently we show one-line crumbs `Home / Models / Model 12345`. If we implement anchor swap, breadcrumbs should reflect the panel too: `Home / Models / Model 12345 / Metrics` — can be clickable to collapse back.
maya: good call. Also thinking about deep link shareability: if someone copies the URL with `#deploy` we should include a `?share=1` fade-in that highlights the element for a few seconds so recipients notice where to look.
kevin: prefer adding a short `?prefill=1` is weird. `?highlight=deploy` makes intent explicit.
maya: sure — `?highlight=deploy`. UX: animation duration should be subtle. Devs: any perf implications for large pages with continuous batching (lots of components)?
devon: large DOM could slow scroll. We should lazy-render panels and when `panel=metrics` is present render it first, or prerender minimal anchor area. Also ensure `scrollIntoView({behavior:'auto'})` for immediate focus when appropriate.
sam: routing edgecase: if a user lands with `panel=metrics#deploy` but model 12345 is not in cache, we need to wait for model load then perform anchor focus. Need to show skeleton and no jump until ready. Add a client-side guard.
maya: noted — add skeleton + aria-busy. I'll add that to the pattern doc.
route-bot: Automated check: deep-link pattern `(/console/.+)/:id` + `panel` param + optional `#anchor` validated. Found 2 other routes sharing similar pattern: `/console/dedicated/*` and `/console/private/*` — consider centralizing handler.
kevin: central handler is good. Also add analytics event `nav.deep_link` with fields `target_path`, `panel`, `anchor`, `expanded_from_state` for A/Bing rollout.
anna: accessibility QA items: keyboard-only test flow, screenreader regression test, focus ring visible after programmatic focus, and ensure skip links still work when groups expanded via deep link.
devon: one more: URL canonicalization for trailing slash and case sensitivity. Normalize to lowercase IDs and strip trailing slashes to reduce duplicates.
maya: great list. I'll update the console IA PR with: canonical URL contract, focus management snippets, skeleton loading flow, and analytics spec. Can folks review the PR once I open it later today?
kevin: yep.
sam: will check router fallback behaviour.
anna: i'll run accessibility smoke tests.
devon: happy to review perf implications.
maya: thanks — will post PR link shortly :sparkles:
